title: Database manifest
description: The manifest of a typed node of type `database` (docs/DESIGN.md, sections 8.1 to 8.5; decisions 14 to 19). It is the node content: each change is a new version of the node (encoding `typed_manifest_v1`). The data lives in the engine, not in the manifest. A control loop makes the real database equal to the manifest and reports the status. Step 2 accepts only the engines `postgres` and `sqlite` and the plan `shared-small`. DRAFT for review (step 2 specify phase).

manifest_version.description: The version of this schema. Missing means 1.

engine.description: The database engine (decision 14). `document`, `search`, `vector` and `kv` of section 8.1 come later; until then they fail validation.

version.description: The major version of the engine. Postgres: "17" (the version of the shared cluster). SQLite: "3". A change of the major version is a planned operation, not a manifest edit, in step 2: a different value from the running one fails with `validation_failed`.

plan.description: The placement (section 8.3). Only `shared-small` in step 2 (decision 16: dedicated plans later). Its limits (size, connections, statement timeout, row cap) come from the tenant plan (section 4.3), not from the manifest.

extensions.description: Postgres extensions to create in the database. Only names on the allow-list of the cluster are valid; `anon` (PostgreSQL Anonymizer) is managed by Ruum and is not listed here. Must be empty for `sqlite`.

backups.description: Backups (decision 17: point-in-time restore for 7 days). Step 2 accepts only 7.

data_classes.description: The CONFIRMED data class of each column (section 8.5). The key is `<schema>.<table>.<column>` (SQLite: `main.<table>.<column>`), with each part quoted as in SQL when it contains a dot or a quote. A column that is not listed counts as `personal` (fail safe). Only a person changes this map: `confirmColumnClasses` writes a new manifest version, and `updateDatabaseManifest` from an agent may not change it (agents suggest classes with `suggestColumnClasses` or in a migration).

migrations.description: Where the declared migrations live (decision 19), as a path relative to the database node's parent folder, for example `migrations/`. The platform runs them in name order at deploy time and rolls back the one that fails. Optional in step 2: migrations can also be sent with `applyDatabaseMigration`.

template.description: Set by the platform when the database was made from a template (section 2.7) or is a branch: the source node and its manifest version. Read-only for clients.

DataClass.description: `normal`: shown as is. `personal` (names, emails, phones, addresses, free text): agents see consistent pseudonyms. `secret` (tokens, password hashes): agents see that the column exists; a non-empty value is the hidden-value marker.
